# 1. Read Data (SKIP IF YOU DO NOT NEED TO PULL FROM ORACLE)

Confidential data: Store locally in the confidential data folder - This folder is excluded using gitignore and will not push to the GitHub repo. If intermediate data (shapefiles etc.) are needed, please put them in data\>intermediate - Filename should use the syntax rootname_descriptivename

# 2. Clean data and create time series csv

Transform the data to fit the IEA data format.
For more info on IEA data format go to the IEAnalyzeR vignette [HERE](https://gulf-iea.github.io/IEAnalyzeR/articles/How_to_use_IEAnalyzeR.html).
Once data are formatted with time (annual or monthly) as column 1 and metric values in the remaining columns, you can use the function convert_cleaned_data to convert your csv into a format that can be read by the data_prep function. Replace "your_data" in the code below with whatever your dataframe is called.

```{r}
ACL.gulf = readRDS(here("data/intermediate/gulf_rec_landings_raw.rds"))



#Now let's just get a list of all the species in the dataset and their total landings
gulf_specs = ACL.gulf %>% 
  group_by(NEW_COM) %>% 
  summarize(
    GOM_LABEL = first(GOM_LABEL),
    total_landings = sum(LBSEST_SECWWT, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>% 
  arrange(GOM_LABEL, NEW_COM)

write_csv(gulf_specs, here("data/intermediate/gulf_rec_landings_species_list.csv"))

```

```{r}
clean_data <- ACL.gulf %>%
  filter(!is.na(YEAR))
```

clean the dataset to only keep species within Gulf Council Finfish FMPs, the Coastal Migratory Pelagics (CMP) FMP, and the red drum FMP. 
https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/species/federally-managed-gulf-america-reef-fish
https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/management-plan/gulf-and-south-atlantic-coastal-migratory-pelagic-fishery-management-plan 
https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/management-plan/gulf-red-drum-fishery-management-plan 
```{r}
# Strictly verified GMFMC-managed finfish species
gmfmc_finfish_official <- c(
  # Reef Fish FMP - Snappers
  "red snapper", "vermilion snapper", "gray snapper", "lane snapper", 
  "mutton snapper", "yellowtail snapper", "cubera snapper", "silk snapper", 
  "blackfin snapper", "queen snapper", "wenchman",
  
  # Reef Fish FMP - Groupers
  "gag", "red grouper", "scamp", "yellowedge grouper", 
  "black grouper", "yellowfin grouper", "yellowmouth grouper", 
  "snowy grouper", "warsaw grouper", "goliath grouper", "nassau grouper", "speckled hind",
  
  # Reef Fish FMP - Tilefishes
  "golden tilefish", "blueline tilefish", "goldface tilefish",
  
  # Reef Fish FMP - Jacks
  "greater amberjack", "lesser amberjack", "almaco jack", "banded rudderfish",
  
  # Reef Fish FMP - Others
  "gray triggerfish", "hogfish", 
  
  # Coastal Migratory Pelagics (CMP) FMP
  "king mackerel", "spanish mackerel", "cobia",
  
  # Red Drum FMP
  "red drum"
)

# Filter landings to strictly official GMFMC finfish

dat_managed <- clean_data %>%
  filter(NEW_COM %in% gmfmc_finfish_official,
         YEAR < 2026)

managed_finfish <- dat_managed %>% 
  group_by(YEAR) %>%
   mutate(
    land_mil_lbs = LBSEST_SECWWT / 1e6,
  ) %>% 
  summarise(
    total_mil_lbs = sum(land_mil_lbs, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>% 
  select(YEAR, total_mil_lbs)

write_csv(dat_managed, here("data/intermediate/managed_species_landings_by_species_rec.csv"))
write_csv(managed_finfish, here("data/intermediate/gulf_managed_species_rec_landings_1981_present.csv"))
```


### Unmanaged species

Had Gemini give me code to add a column to the dataset to group all of the species into categories

```{r}
# Add the 'category' column using case_when
df_categorized <- clean_data %>%
  mutate(
    # Normalize species name to lowercase and strip special whitespace characters
    sp = str_to_lower(str_squish(gsub("\u00a0", " ", coalesce(NEW_COM, ""))))
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    category = case_when(
      # Empty / NA rows
      sp == "" ~ "other",
      
      # ------------------------------------------------------------------
      # 1. INVERTEBRATES
      # ------------------------------------------------------------------
      sp %in% c("chloeia viridis", "hypogastrura glancei") |
        grepl("crab|shrimp|lobster|squid|octopus|clam|oyster|scallop|snail|conch|worm", sp) & 
        !grepl("eel|toadfish|blenny|goby|fish", sp) ~ "invertebrate",

      # ------------------------------------------------------------------
      # 2. OTHER / UNIDENTIFIED / AMBIGUOUS AGGREGATES
      # ------------------------------------------------------------------
      sp %in% c(
        "cartilaginous fishes", "bass genus", "trout family",
        "unidentified fish", "unidentified catfishes", "unidentified eel",
        "unidentified bottom fish", "unidentified surface fish",
        "unidentified sharks", "unidentified skate or ray",
        "unidentified flounder or sole", "NA", "unidentified grouper"
      ) ~ "other",

      # ------------------------------------------------------------------
      # 3. FRESHWATER TAXA
      # (Exclude coastal marine catfishes: gafftopsail & hardhead)
      # ------------------------------------------------------------------
      grepl("gafftopsail|hardhead", sp) ~ "coastal",
      sp %in% c(
        "largemouth bass", "smallmouth bass", "spotted bass", "warmouth",
        "bluegill", "black crappie", "crappie genus", "bowfin", "bigmouth buffalo",
        "chain pickerel", "common carp", "silver carp", "western mosquitofish",
        "inland silverside", "freshwater drum", "cichlid family"
      ) |
        grepl("catfish|bullhead", sp) |
        grepl("\\bgar\\b|gar family|gar genus", sp) |
        grepl("tilapia|sunfish", sp) ~ "freshwater",

      # ------------------------------------------------------------------
      # 4. MARINE PELAGIC (Open water / Oceanic / Epipelagic Migratory)
      # ------------------------------------------------------------------
      grepl("tuna|albacore|bluefin|yellowfin|blackfin|skipjack|bonito", sp) ~ "marine_pelagic",
      grepl("mackerel|wahoo|cero", sp) ~ "marine_pelagic",
      grepl("billfish|marlin|sailfish|spearfish|swordfish", sp) ~ "marine_pelagic",
      grepl("dolphin|mahi|pompano dolphin", sp) ~ "marine_pelagic",
      grepl("flyingfish|barracuda|sennet|escolar|oilfish|barrelfish|pomfret", sp) ~ "marine_pelagic",
      grepl("cobia|rainbow runner|blue runner|scad|pilotfish|rudderfish|almaco jack", sp) ~ "marine_pelagic",
      grepl("amberjack|cottonmouth jack|black jack", sp) ~ "marine_pelagic",
      grepl("blue shark|mako|thresher|oceanic whitetip|silky shark|dusky shark", sp) ~ "marine_pelagic",
      grepl("devil ray|manta|antenna codlet|ribbonfish|oarfish", sp) ~ "marine_pelagic",
      grepl("cutlassfish", sp) ~ "marine_pelagic",

      # ------------------------------------------------------------------
      # 5. COASTAL (Inshore, Estuarine, Surf, Bays, Salt Marsh)
      # ------------------------------------------------------------------
      grepl("red drum|black drum|spotted seatrout|sand seatrout|silver seatrout|seatrout", sp) ~ "coastal",
      grepl("croaker|spot|kingfish genus|southern kingfish|gulf kingfish|northern kingfish|silver perch|bairdiella", sp) ~ "coastal",
      grepl("snook|tarpon|ladyfish|bonefish|permit|florida pompano|palometa|irish pompano", sp) ~ "coastal",
      grepl("sheepshead|pinfish|pigfish|spadefish|tripletail|crevalle jack|leatherjack", sp) ~ "coastal",
      grepl("mullet|menhaden|thread herring|alewife|shad|silverside|anchovy|sardine|scaled sardine", sp) ~ "coastal",
      grepl("mojarra|killifish|topminnow|sheepshead minnow|molly|halfbeak|ballyhoo|balao", sp) ~ "coastal",
      grepl("needlefish|houndfish|pipefish|seahorse", sp) ~ "coastal",
      grepl("stingray|cownose ray|bullnose ray|eagle ray|guitarfish|sawfish", sp) ~ "coastal",
      grepl("blacktip shark|spinner shark|bonnethead|bull shark|sharpnose shark|finetooth shark|lemon shark", sp) ~ "coastal",

      # ------------------------------------------------------------------
      # 6. MARINE DEMERSAL (Reef, Shelf, Benthic & Slope Fishes)
      # ------------------------------------------------------------------
      grepl("snapper|grouper|sea bass|sand perch|scamp|gag|hind|coney|tatus|wenchman|schoolmaster", sp) ~ "marine_demersal",
      grepl("flounder|sole|tonguefish|whiff|halibut|flatfish", sp) ~ "marine_demersal",
      grepl("tilefish|grunt|margate|tomtate|cottonwick|porgy|scup|calamus", sp) ~ "marine_demersal",
      grepl("triggerfish|filefish|boxfish|trunkfish|cowfish|puffer|burrfish|balloonfish", sp) ~ "marine_demersal",
      grepl("searobin|lizardfish|toadfish|midshipman|batfish|frogfish|sargassumfish|stargazer", sp) ~ "marine_demersal",
      grepl("cusk-eel|moray|snake eel|worm eel|conger|academy eel|brotula|pearlfish|slimehead", sp) ~ "marine_demersal",
      grepl("angelfish|butterflyfish|damselfish|beaugregory|reeffish|wrasse|hogfish|razorfish|parrotfish", sp) ~ "marine_demersal",
      grepl("tang|surgeonfish|doctorfish|goby|blenny|jawfish|cardinalfish|soldierfish|squirrelfish|bigeye", sp) ~ "marine_demersal",
      grepl("hake|codlet|rosefish|scorpionfish|lionfish|cornetfish|trumpetfish|gurnard", sp) ~ "marine_demersal",
      grepl("skate|electric ray|torpedo|skate or ray|smoothhound|dogfish|nurse shark|cat shark|angel shark|sand tiger|hammerhead", sp) ~ "marine_demersal",

      # ------------------------------------------------------------------
      # DEFAULT FALLBACK
      # ------------------------------------------------------------------
      TRUE ~ "other"
    )
  ) %>%
  select(-sp)

# 3. Quick verification of the counts per category
print(table(df_categorized$category, useNA = "always"))
```

Let's go back to the clean_data and filter for the unmanaged species we want to plot. First some diagnostics.

```{r}
unmanaged_all = df_categorized %>% 
  filter(category %in% c("coastal", "marine_demersal", "marine_pelagic")) %>% 
  filter(YEAR < 2026)

# Cumulative Landings Pareto Analysis
pareto_df <- unmanaged_all %>%
  group_by(NEW_COM) %>%
  mutate(
    land_mil_lbs = LBSEST_SECWWT / 1e6,
  ) %>% 
  summarise(
    total_mil_lbs = sum(land_mil_lbs, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(total_mil_lbs)) %>%
  mutate(
    RANK = row_number(),
    CUM_LBS = cumsum(total_mil_lbs),
    CUM_PCT = (CUM_LBS / sum(total_mil_lbs)) * 100
  )


# Sensitivity Analysis: Plot trajectories using Top 5, Top 10, Top 15, vs Top 25
top10_spp  <- pareto_df %>% filter(RANK <= 10) %>% pull(NEW_COM)
top20_spp <- pareto_df %>% filter(RANK <= 20) %>% pull(NEW_COM)
top30_spp <- pareto_df %>% filter(RANK <= 30) %>% pull(NEW_COM)
top40_spp <- pareto_df %>% filter(RANK <= 40) %>% pull(NEW_COM)

sensitivity_df <- unmanaged_all %>%
  filter(NEW_COM %in% top40_spp) %>%
  mutate(
    Cutoff = case_when(
      NEW_COM %in% top10_spp ~ "Top 10 Species",
      NEW_COM %in% top20_spp ~ "Top 20 Species",
      NEW_COM %in% top30_spp ~ "Top 30 Species",
      TRUE ~ "Top 40 Species"
    )
  ) %>%
  group_by(YEAR, Cutoff) %>%
  summarise(total_mil_lbs = sum(LBSEST_SECWWT / 1e6, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

# Plot sensitivity curves
ggplot(sensitivity_df, aes(x = YEAR, y = total_mil_lbs, color = Cutoff)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.1) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma_format()) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(1980, 2025, by = 5)) +
  labs(
    title = "Sensitivity of Unmanaged Finfish Trajectory to Taxonomic Scope",
    subtitle = "Testing cumulative volume thresholds (Top 10 vs 20 vs 30 vs 40 species)",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Live Landings (Millions of Pounds)",
    color = "Inclusion Threshold"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))

```

Ok now we have a better handle on which species are the major commercially harvested unmanaged species.

Pull out the species that make up 95% of the landings.

```{r}
top_spec_list = pareto_df %>% 
  filter(CUM_PCT <= 95) %>% 
  pull(NEW_COM)
```

Now we can get the unmanaged data!

```{r}
# Filter landings 
dat_unmanaged <- unmanaged_all %>%
  filter(
    NEW_COM %in% c(top_spec_list)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    total_mil_lbs = LBSEST_SECWWT / 1e6,
    
    # Assign species category for conditional grouping
    Species_Type = case_when(
      category == "coastal"   ~ "Coastal",
      category == "marine_demersal"   ~ "Marine Demersal",
      category == "marine_pelagic"   ~ "Marine Pelagic"
    )
  )

# 2. Summarize annual totals into 3 distinct columns
unmanaged_summary <- dat_unmanaged %>% 
  group_by(YEAR) %>%
  summarise(
    coast_mil_lbs     = sum(total_mil_lbs[Species_Type == "Coastal"], na.rm = TRUE),
    dem_mil_lbs     = sum(total_mil_lbs[Species_Type == "Marine Demersal"], na.rm = TRUE),
    pel_mil_lbs     = sum(total_mil_lbs[Species_Type == "Marine Pelagic"], na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>% 
  select(YEAR, coast_mil_lbs, dem_mil_lbs, pel_mil_lbs)

# Save intermediate summary CSVs
write_csv(dat_unmanaged, here("data/intermediate/rec_unmanaged_species_landings_by_species.csv"))
write_csv(unmanaged_summary, here("data/intermediate/rec_unmanaged_species_landings.csv"))
```

In case we just want an overall plot 
```{r}
# Filter landings to both food and bait lists & adjust for inflation
dat_unmanaged_overall <- unmanaged_all %>%
  filter(
    NEW_COM %in% c(top_spec_list)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    total_mil_lbs = LBSEST_SECWWT / 1e6
  )

# 2. Summarize annual totals 
unmanaged_summary_overall <- dat_unmanaged_overall %>% 
  group_by(YEAR) %>%
  summarise(
    total_mil_lbs = sum(total_mil_lbs, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>% 
  select(YEAR, total_mil_lbs)

```

# 4. Create Data_Prep object

Please use your formatted csv to create a "data_prep" object.
For more info on the data_prep function see the vignette linked above.
```{r}
data_obj1<-IEAnalyzeR::data_prep(csv_filename1)
data_obj2<-IEAnalyzeR::data_prep(csv_filename2)
data_obj3<-IEAnalyzeR::data_prep(csv_filename3)
```

# 5. Save Formatted data_prep object

This will save your data to the appropriate folder.
```{r}
saveRDS(data_obj1, file = object_filename1)

saveRDS(data_obj3, file = object_filename3)
```
